A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CaptionQA and contain complete, readable main text and supplementary material. Text, equations, tables and figures can be matched reliably; pagination changes do not indicate missing content.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of captioning models, QA-reader comparisons, annotation-quality measurements and supplementary prompt, category and ranking-stability analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including the main comparisons in Tables 2–4 and detailed model results in supplementary Tables 11–26.

M1.justification: The taxonomy-guided benchmark construction, question generation and filtering, caption-only QA procedure and scoring scheme remain unchanged in Sections 3–4. No algorithm or model component is added or revised.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same Natural, Document, E-commerce and Embodied AI coverage. Table 1 retains 657 images, 33,027 questions, 25 top-level categories and 69 subcategories.

E2.justification: Comparator membership remains unchanged in the captioning, QA-reader and image-versus-caption experiments. Tables 12–14 rename InternVL3 to InternVL3-14B, but the corresponding rows already specified size 14B in v1.

E3.justification: The four caption prompts, evaluation metrics, option shuffling, fixed caption pool for reader comparisons and 50-question-per-domain quality audits are unchanged. No new experimental protocol or revised setting is reported.

E4.justification: The prompt-transition, dataset-size sensitivity, category-level, difficulty and qualitative analyses are retained, including supplementary Sections 11 and 14–17. Removing a summary sentence from Section 5.2 does not remove the underlying analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions report three temperature-zero runs for QA-reader stability, ten sampling trials per subset size for ranking stability, and the same across-model descriptive statistics in Table 9. Uncertainty reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: Matched tables and figures retain their numerical results and rankings. For example, Table 3 reports the same Simple-prompt overall scores of 90.29% for GPT-5 and 87.02% for Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B. Supplementary result entries are unchanged apart from model-label clarification.

T1.justification: The caption-only QA formulation and piecewise scoring definition are mathematically identical in both PDFs. Apparent equation differences in text extraction disappear on visual inspection; no assumptions, derivations or proofs are added.

C1.justification: The utility-based caption benchmark, cross-domain diagnostic coverage, caption-versus-image utility gap and extensible construction pipeline remain the core contributions. The added related-work sentence clarifies this existing contribution without expanding its scientific scope.

C2.justification: Section 5.2 removes the explicit interpretation that additional caption length mainly adds noise rather than useful signal. The diminishing-returns conclusion, domain-specific bottleneck explanations and supporting Section 14 analyses remain, making this a limited reduction in interpretive emphasis.

D1.justification: v1 provides a direct code-repository link in the abstract; v2 replaces it with a project-page link beneath the affiliations. Implementation, hardware and cost details remain unchanged. The PDFs establish a changed access pointer, not changed resource availability.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds an explicit positioning statement distinguishing the downstream-driven definition and evaluation objective from merely switching between statement judging and QA. This modestly sharpens the comparison with prior approaches; all 47 cited works remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Edits include the Section 2 clarification, shortened Section 5.2 discussion, small grammatical changes, an author-affiliation update and model-label normalization. Section 13 also changes 'Rationale' to 'Rational'. The overall narrative and section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 4 moves from PDF page 8 to page 7, the conclusion and references reflow, a project-link line is added and printed page numbers are removed. Figures and table structures otherwise retain their existing content and design.

improvement.justification: v2 makes the existing contribution slightly more explicit and trims one stronger interpretation, while preserving the benchmark, methods, results and full supporting analyses. These limited editorial gains, minor wording regressions and layout changes do not materially alter overall quality. The replacement resource link alone does not establish improved reproducibility.
